capabilities: drag files and folders from the File Explorer as path text
copy the dragged path text to the clipboard as a fallback
configure absolute vs vault-relative paths and shell quoting
separate multiple selected paths with space or newline
append a trailing space so paths fit into commands
extras: Desktop only; does not run on mobile. Drop support depends on the receiving terminal accepting text/plain data, and the File Explorer DOM it relies on may break after Obsidian updates.
motivation: The author built it because file tree dragging is not optimized for terminal workflows when the vault doubles as a project notebook, AI context library, or operating console.
problem: Obsidian's file tree delivers an internal drag object when dragged out, so passing note or folder paths into terminal and shell workflows is not direct.

relations.evidence: It is designed for people who use Obsidian next to Terminal.app, iTerm2, Termy, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI
relations.plugin: Terminal.app, iTerm2, Termy, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI

requires.name: a terminal that accepts text/plain drops

summary: Drag-and-drop helper that turns File Explorer drags into terminal-ready absolute or vault-relative path text, with a clipboard fallback.
